topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides introductory framing and outlines the lecture's focus on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Principles of innate immune recognition via PAMPs, DAMPs, and PRRs
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the fundamental criteria and cellular localization principles by which innate immune receptors identify microbial presence and tissue damage.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptor families, signaling, and inflammasome activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the major classes of pattern recognition receptors, their downstream intracellular signaling mechanisms, and the molecular assembly required to process inflammatory cytokines.

topics.label: Inflammatory mediator release, leukocyte recruitment, and systemic pathology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how activated sentinel cells drive immune cell migration into tissues and the lymphatic system, as well as the life-threatening consequences when these systemic responses become dysregulated.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic adaptations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the mechanisms that terminate inflammatory responses, restore damaged tissue, and manage unresolved infections through chronic inflammatory structures.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the topic of the following session.
